\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಉಜ್ಜು} (ujju)}{ಉಜ್ಜು (ujju)}]{\kn{ಉಜ್ಜು} (ujju) — to scrub, to rub, to brush (teeth)}

\label{lesson:KA-C198-ujju}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a headmaster, then the Kannada for a secretary.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಉಜ್ಜು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಉಜ್ಜು}} — \emph{ujju} — \textquotedblleft{}to scrub, to rub, to brush (teeth)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಉಜ್ಜು}} (\emph{ujju}) is native Dravidian, one word with Tamil \emph{urai} and Telugu \emph{ora} (DEDR 665). DEDR lists \emph{urdu}, \emph{uddu}, \emph{ujju}, \textquotedblleft{}to rub\textquotedblright{}. DEDR 665 compares, with a query, Sanskrit \emph{uñch}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ujju}, once more

\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಬಿಡು} (biḍu)}{ಬಿಡು (biḍu)}]{\kn{ಬಿಡು} (biḍu) — to let go, to leave}

\label{lesson:KA-C198-bidu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for to carry away, then the Kannada for to hold.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಬಿಡು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಬಿಡು}} — \emph{biḍu} — \textquotedblleft{}to let go, to leave\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಬಿಡು}} (\emph{biḍu}) is native Dravidian, one word with Tamil \emph{viṭu} (DEDR 5393). DEDR lists \emph{biḍu} itself, \textquotedblleft{}to let loose, leave\textquotedblright{}: the old \emph{v-} has become \emph{b-}. DEDR 5393 notes that Sanskrit \emph{avamocana}, \textquotedblleft{}inn\textquotedblright{}, is a calque of Tamil \emph{viṭuti}, \textquotedblleft{}lodging place\textquotedblright{}, from this root.
\end{cousinweb}
